text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
Run PR-Agent in dry-run mode on a single low-traffic branch in the main repo.

It tests the tool’s real impact without risking live PRs. If it works, we scale it to high-traffic branches. If it fails, we only waste one branch.

name: Gauge
text: Dry-run normalizes noise—it hides the signal PR-Agent’s dr misses. Instead, run it on a *closed* PR where the tool’s feedback can’t pollute live branches, and we can measure real impact by how many review points it actually catches.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent on a *merged* PR with known issues to measure real catch-rate without risking live branches. This tests the tool’s ability to surface *actionable* feedback, not just noise, while avoiding the dry-run’s false negatives.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent on a merged PR with known issues. This tests real catch-rate without risking live branches or polluting active reviews. The trade-off is delayed feedback—we won’t see results until after the PR merges—but we avoid false negatives from dry-run and measure actual value. If it catches meaningful issues, we scale it to high-traffic branches. If not, we drop it without harm.
